### Summary

The Python package `kintera` is a pybind11 extension built over the C++ options and modules of
@sec-ch11-options. Options classes keep the C++ names and the C++ getter and setter pairs; modules are bound as
`torch` modules, so they move between devices and dtypes like any `torch.nn.Module`. A Python driver therefore
builds the same objects as a C++ driver, from the same YAML file.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Expose the options, modules and free functions of kintera to Python.

**Data.** `torch` tensors in, `torch` tensors out; shapes as in @sec-ch11-options.

**Placement.** Imported once; `import kintera` also registers the packaged data directory.

**Activation.** Always.

**Guarantee / limits.** Binding signatures follow the C++ ones; see the Code layer.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer.
:::

A typical call sequence is `KineticsOptions.from_yaml(file)`, then `Kinetics(options)`, then `forward` or
`forward_with_rate_constants`, then `jacobian`, then `evolve_implicit`.

### Derivation

No derivation: this scheme is an interface.

### Numerical method

No numerical method and no figure: this scheme is an interface.

### Code

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| module entry | {{< code python/csrc/kintera.cpp >}} | `PYBIND11_MODULE` | always |
| binding macros | {{< code python/csrc/pyoptions.hpp >}} | `ADD_OPTION` | always |
| kinetics bindings | {{< code python/csrc/pykinetics.cpp bind_kinetics >}} | `bind_kinetics` | always |
| thermo bindings | {{< code python/csrc/pythermo.cpp bind_thermo >}} | `bind_thermo` | always |

: Code map of the Python bindings. {#tbl-ch11-python-api-code}

The binding is built in these steps:

1. The module entry ({{< code python/csrc/kintera.cpp >}}) defines the free functions `atomic_mass`,
   `molar_mass`, `molar_masses`, `molar_masses_from_yaml` and `nasa9_gibbs_rt`, the classes `SpeciesThermo` and
   `Reaction`, and the KINETICS reader types, then calls `bind_thermo`, `bind_constants`, `bind_kinetics`,
   `bind_photolysis`, `bind_diffusion`, `bind_sparse_solver` and `bind_equilibrium`.
2. The same file defines the registry accessors (`species_names`, `set_species_names`, and the same pair for
   weights, `cref_R`, `uref_R` and `sref_R`), the resource functions `set_search_paths`, `get_search_paths`,
   `add_resource_directory` and `find_resource`, and the solvers `evolve_implicit`, `evolve_ros2` and `ros2_k1`.
3. `ADD_OPTION(T, struct, name)` ({{< code python/csrc/pyoptions.hpp >}}) binds the `ADD_ARG` getter and setter
   of one field under one Python name, with reference return policy. `ADD_KINTERA_MODULE` in the same file binds
   a module with a default constructor, a constructor from options, the read-only `options`, `module(name)`,
   `buffer(name)` and `forward`.
4. `bind_kinetics` ({{< code python/csrc/pykinetics.cpp bind_kinetics >}}) binds one options class per rate form
   and the `KineticsOptions` class, with the static constructors `from_yaml(filename, verbose=False)`,
   `from_kinetics_base(...)` and `from_kinetics_base_pun(...)`, and the `Kinetics` module. `Kinetics.forward`
   and `Kinetics.forward_with_rate_constants` release the GIL; `forward_nogil` is a second name for the same
   call. `Kinetics.jacobian` takes `temp`, `conc`, `cvol`, `rate`, `rc_ddC`, and the optional `rc_ddT` and
   `rate_constants`.
5. `bind_thermo` ({{< code python/csrc/pythermo.cpp bind_thermo >}}) binds `NucleationOptions`, `ThermoOptions`
   (with `from_yaml`, `Tref`, `Pref`, `nucleation`, `max_iter`, `ftol` and `uv_solver`) and two modules:
   `ThermoY.forward(rho, intEng, yfrac, warm_start=False, diag=None)` and
   `ThermoX.forward(temp, pres, xfrac, warm_start=False, diag=None)`. `ThermoX` adds `effective_cp`,
   `extrapolate_dlnp` and `extrapolate_dz`; `ThermoY` adds `take_saturation_adjustment_failures`. Both add
   `compute(ab, args)`.
6. On import, the Python package adds its own `data` directory to the resource search path
   (`_add_packaged_resource_directory`, {{< code python/__init__.py _add_packaged_resource_directory >}}).

A Python use of the kinetics bindings, from the test {{< code tests/test_kinetics_null_options.py >}}, is not
quoted in this draft.

### Limits

- `ThermoX.extrapolate_dlnp` and `extrapolate_dz` are lambdas in the binding that build `ExtrapOptions`; their
  options are not reachable from YAML. Read from {{< code python/csrc/pythermo.cpp bind_thermo >}}.
- The stub file and the bindings are kept in step by hand; whether they agree at the pin is not checked here.
